name: team-profile

capacity.note: twelve is the ceiling in any composition, and only `bench` holds them — the default three-up seats six (a seventh reflows it to four columns; a ninth wants `bench`, which drops the notes)

density.note: one clause on what this person owns, not a paragraph — and the count includes the name and the image reference beside it, so about four of the allowance is fixed cost before a word of prose

description: A roster of named people, each under a portrait, with the role they own.
purpose: Use for the people slide — 'meet the leaders', 'your account team', the QBR roll-call. Each person is a portrait, a name, a role and one line. Anyone with no photo gets a monogram of their initials instead, so a half-photographed roster still reads as one designed wall rather than a set of holes: the monogram stays quiet beside real faces, and takes a categorical hue only when nobody in the roster has a photo.

eyebrow.description: Optional kicker above the headline — a short label in backticks, e.g. `Your account team`.

title.description: Optional headline above the roster. A claim earns its place ('Six people own this program end to end'); a bare label ('The team') does not.

people.description: One top-level bullet per person, and the bullet IS their name. Everything about them nests under it.

portrait.description: The person's photo, nested under their name as `- ![](photo.jpg)`. Leave the alt empty — the name beside it is the accessible label. Omit it entirely and the engine draws a monogram from the initials instead.

role.description: The one backticked nested line is the role, set as a small tracked label under the name — `` `Head of Delivery` ``. Deliberately not a pill: a boxed chip under every one of twelve faces competes with the portraits it is meant to caption.

note.description: Any remaining plain nested line is the note: one short line on what this person owns.

side.description: `sides` only. Two `### ` subheadings, each followed by its own list, label the two rosters ('Your team' / 'Our team').

commonMistakes.mistake: Leading with the portrait instead of the name.
commonMistakes.fix: The top-level bullet is the person's NAME (`- Ada Okafor`); the portrait, role and note all nest under it. Writing `- ![](ada.jpg)` at the top level makes the photo the person and leaves the card with no name.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing the role as plain nested text instead of backticks.
commonMistakes.fix: The one backticked nested line is the role, set as the label under the name. Written plain it becomes a second note line, so the card shows two body lines and no role.

commonMistakes.mistake: Filling the alt text on the portrait.
commonMistakes.fix: Write `![](photo.jpg)` with an empty alt. The name is set right beside the face and IS the accessible label, so alt text only makes a screen reader say it twice — the engine drops it either way.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a KEY INSIGHT or a closing note to a full six-person roster.
commonMistakes.fix: The coda cell takes its height out of the stage, so the second row clips. Drop to four people, move the line into the headline, or switch to `bench`, whose rows are half the height.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: Three to six people who each need a face, a role and one line — the workhorse 'meet the team' roster.
One person is accountable and the rest report into the work: the hero cell and the rule beneath it say so without a sentence.
The roster runs past eight and the notes matter less than the breadth — six up, face and role only.
Two teams meet: the QBR roll-call, a joint steering group, a vendor and a client side that need labelling.
Four or fewer leaders who each need a real line, and the roles read better scanned down a column than centered under a face.
